FM-01.title: Read and combine
FM-01.hint: Read the two parts in order. A missing final newline affects how concatenation joins them.

FM-02.title: Write a handover
FM-02.hint: Compare replacement with append redirection. Inspect the finished file for any stale line.

FM-03.title: Search a long document
FM-03.hint: Search within the pager and distinguish the active instruction from the retired one.

FM-04.title: Read the bookends
FM-04.hint: Request explicit line counts from the beginning and the end, then preserve that order.

FM-05.title: Restore time order
FM-05.hint: Reverse the records while keeping the characters within each record unchanged.

FM-06.title: Count real failures
FM-06.hint: A matching word in the middle is not the same as a matching record prefix. Count selected lines.

FM-07.title: Pair aligned columns
FM-07.hint: These inputs correspond by line position. Preserve a tab between each pair of values.

FM-08.title: Match records by ID
FM-08.hint: Matching by key needs consistently sorted inputs. Row position is not a student identity.

FM-09.title: Search the workshop board with grep
FM-09.hint: Brackets have a special meaning in a regular expression. Match the bench label literally and check the state at the start of each record.

FO-01.title: Private notes
FO-01.hint: Compare the owner, group and other permission sets. Remove only the access the task forbids.

FO-02.title: Team reference
FO-02.hint: Add the read, write and execute values for each permission class before choosing a numeric mode.

FO-03.title: Directory traversal
FO-03.hint: Listing names and accessing a file inside a directory require different directory permissions.

FO-04.title: Return a misplaced file
FO-04.hint: An owner change and a group change are separate operations. Preserve the fields the task does not ask to change.

FO-05.title: Share with the right team
FO-05.hint: Compare the file group with your memberships. Group read bits help only the matching group.

FO-06.title: Hand over an archive
FO-06.hint: Check owner, group and mode together. Consider when you will still have permission to change the file.

FO-07.title: Keep new files in the team
FO-07.hint: A shared directory can control the group inherited by new files. Special directory bits differ from ordinary execute bits.

LD-01.title: The single dash
LD-01.hint: Some filename arguments also have a special meaning for standard input. Consider how a relative path changes the argument.

LD-02.title: The awkward handover name
LD-02.hint: Quoting keeps spaces in one argument. A filename starting with dashes also needs to be handled as a path rather than an option.

LD-03.title: The apparently empty folder
LD-03.hint: An ordinary listing leaves out names beginning with a dot. Explore the listing options before deciding a directory is empty.

LD-04.title: The readable record
LD-04.hint: Inspect file types before printing unknown contents. Dash-prefixed names still need careful path handling.

LD-05.title: The exact archive record
LD-05.hint: Combine regular-file, exact byte-size, and executable-status tests, then inspect the remaining file types. A partial match is a decoy.

LD-06.title: The misplaced teacher record
LD-06.hint: Owner and owning group are separate search conditions. Combine both with the size; permission errors are written to a different stream from results.

LD-07.title: The line that occurs once
LD-07.hint: Group identical lines before counting them. Keeping one copy of every distinct value also keeps values that originally repeated.

NM-01.title: Discover the practice network
NM-01.hint: Use discovery without port scanning. Both service targets must be up; the scanner and gateway may appear too.

NM-02.title: TCP connect and port states
NM-02.hint: Compare confirmed listeners with a port that actively refuses connections. Use the connect scan type.

NM-03.title: SYN and full port ranges
NM-03.hint: A default port list is not exhaustive. Use SYN scanning across the full TCP range and inspect the extra listener.

NM-04.title: Service and version probes
NM-04.hint: Port-based names are only guesses. Service probes should identify the FTP and SSH products and TLS-wrapped HTTP.

NM-05.title: UDP DNS replies
NM-05.hint: Silence can mean open or filtered. A DNS version reply and service probe provide stronger evidence.

NM-06.title: HTTP titles and headers
NM-06.hint: Use named HTTP scripts to inspect the title and the header describing the site role.

NM-07.title: Crawler rules and HTTP methods
NM-07.hint: Inspect the crawler exclusions and the methods advertised for the practice path. Read the script arguments first.

NM-08.title: TLS certificate names
NM-08.hint: A certificate has subject and alternative names. Inspect both on the HTTPS listener.

NM-09.title: SSH public host keys
NM-09.hint: A host-key fingerprint can be collected without a user login. Include the RSA key.

NM-10.title: Anonymous FTP inventory
NM-10.hint: The mock FTP catalogue permits anonymous read-only listing. Record the handover document without changing files.

NM-11.title: The archive service
NM-11.hint: Return to the second discovered target. Search beyond default ports, then probe the HTTP service and inspect its role.

NM-12.title: Combined service inventory
NM-12.hint: Combine explicit TCP and UDP port sets, service probes and the named scripts. Save all output formats together.

WEB-01.title: The yearbook handover
WEB-01.hint: Start at /robots.txt on the school portal. Find the yearbook proof and compare the printed text with its HTML source.

BF-01.title: The misleading form
BF-01.hint: Discover retired pages, then compare the form with its JavaScript and the actual request. A directory value in browser source may be reversible.

BF-02.title: The helpful login error
BF-02.hint: Hold one credential constant while changing the other. Which response confirms an account exists, and which credential has not yet been checked?

BF-03.title: The shared password gate
BF-03.hint: Do not assume all logins validate in the same order. Compare failures and inspect the retired client's migration notes before deciding what a response proves.

BF-04.title: The hidden management account
BF-04.hint: A crawler exclusion list is not a complete directory inventory. A digest in browser source can be matched against candidate usernames offline before password guesses.

P1-01.title: Private report forms
P1-01.hint: Compare how your report is requested with how other student records are identified. Does the server check who owns the requested record?

P1-02.title: The forgotten console
P1-02.hint: A page missing from the navigation can still be reachable. Pay attention to the portal's operational features.

P1-03.title: Files on the lab box
P1-03.hint: Once inside the web container, practise listing directories and checking which files your account can read.

P2-01.title: The results backup
P2-01.hint: Inventory the lab's loopback services. An exposed backup deserves the same access checks as the main application.

P2-02.title: Internal trust
P2-02.hint: The public ports are only part of the network. Consider what a service inside the lab network assumes about its callers.

P3-01.title: The classmate search
P3-01.hint: Watch how the search responds to unusual input. Ask whether the input is treated strictly as data.

P3-02.title: The student review
P3-02.hint: A student's saved text may later be viewed by staff. Think about where that text is rendered and whose browser renders it.

P3-03.title: Who decides your role?
P3-03.hint: Inspect the browser's session state. Which values decide your identity and role, and what prevents someone from changing them?

P3-04.title: The marks ledger
P3-04.hint: Compare what the interface allows with what the marks endpoint actually checks. A hidden button is only a browser restriction.

P4-01.title: The server diagnostic
P4-01.hint: A diagnostic tool turns user input into a server action. Consider which interpreter receives that input.

P4-02.title: The uploaded asset
P4-02.hint: Follow an uploaded file through its whole lifecycle. The filename check and the way the server later uses the file may disagree.

P4-03.title: The remote school logo
P4-03.hint: When the portal imports a remote resource, the request starts on the server. Which destinations can that server reach?

P4-04.title: The fee receipt
P4-04.hint: Trace a payment from the browser to the ledger. Which amounts and approval decisions does the server calculate for itself?

P5-01.title: The browser configuration
P5-01.hint: Assets delivered to the browser are public to that browser's user. Review what the client is trusted to keep secret.

P5-02.title: Yesterday's configuration
P5-02.hint: The current tree is only one version of the project. Consider whether removing a value from a file removes its earlier copies.

P5-03.title: The dependency inventory
P5-03.hint: Compare pinned dependency versions with published advisories. The labctl audit command can help verify a real finding.

P5-04.title: The helpful error page
P5-04.hint: A failed request can reveal more than a successful one. Notice whether diagnostic details intended for developers reach the browser.

P5B-01.title: The legacy staff account
P5B-01.hint: Legacy authentication may store passwords differently. If you obtain a hash, examine its format and whether it uses a salt.

P5B-02.title: The sealed browser value
P5B-02.hint: Inspect the shape of the supposedly protected browser value. Reversible encoding and encryption provide different guarantees.

P5B-03.title: The signed API token
P5B-03.hint: A signature is only as strong as its secret. Examine the token format and think about how its signing key was chosen.

P5B-04.title: The encrypted transcript
P5B-04.hint: An encrypted value cannot remain secret if its decryption material is delivered alongside it. Review the browser assets.

P5B-05.title: The repeating blocks
P5B-05.hint: Compare repeated portions of the encrypted data. Some encryption modes preserve patterns between identical input blocks.

P5D-01.title: The saved preferences
P5D-01.hint: A browser preference should be plain data. Consider what happens when a server reconstructs an object supplied by the browser.

P5D-02.title: The class representative
P5D-02.hint: A settings form exposes a few fields. Does the server explicitly restrict which account properties a request may update?

P5D-03.title: The account recovery trail
P5D-03.hint: Account recovery creates temporary secrets. Check whether those secrets appear in diagnostic records that other users can reach.

SE-01.title: The staff noticeboard
SE-01.hint: The fictional staff member's public posts form a profile. Look for repeated personal details that might influence a weak password.

SE-02.title: The suspicious inbox
SE-02.hint: Compare the sender, destination links, and requested action in each sample message. Pressure is a clue, not proof on its own.

SE-03.title: The helpdesk conversation
SE-03.hint: Read the fictional staff directory and the scripted helpdesk's requirements. Small public facts may combine into a convincing identity claim.

OSINT-01.title: Which hall is hosting the swap?
OSINT-01.hint: A newer post can repeat an old programme. Look for the organiser's latest notice about the swap, then find the hall's code on the visitor map.

OSINT-02.title: The first photograph credit
OSINT-02.hint: Match the whole caption before comparing timestamps. The credits on the later clippings can confirm the original outlet.

OSINT-03.title: The book returns desk
OSINT-03.hint: Read the volunteers' directions in the notices. On the map, narrow the desks down to ones that touch both named landmarks.

F-01.title: The noticeboard
F-01.hint: The visible picture is only one part of an image file. Examine the information stored around its pixels.

F-02.title: The staff photo
F-02.hint: Compare the file's size with what its dimensions suggest. Is there more data than the image format needs?

F-03.title: The prize-giving photo
F-03.hint: The metadata is clean and no extra file is attached. Small changes within the pixels can carry information.

F-04.title: The school bell
F-04.hint: An animation is a sequence with timing information. Examine its individual frames rather than relying on playback.

F-05.title: The radio call
F-05.hint: The beeps have structure. Look for timing differences, pauses, and a code that can represent digits as well as letters.

F-06.title: The assembly recording
F-06.hint: Listening is only one way to examine sound. Try a visual representation of how its frequencies change over time.

F-07.title: The corridor CCTV
F-07.hint: Six seconds contains many separate images. Check whether ordinary-speed playback hides anything between them.

F-08.title: The first completed print job
F-08.hint: Find the first job that finished printing programme.pdf on the hall printer. Compare completion times and use the job ID.

F-09.title: The print-room reply
F-09.hint: Read the headers to find the message this email answers. Take the part of that ID before the @ and leave out the angle brackets.

F-10.title: The matching programme
F-10.hint: Compare the SHA-256 of each recovered copy with the full digest recorded at collection. Use the matching filename without its extension.

STEG-01.title: The unsigned notice
STEG-01.hint: Inspect the Unicode names of the invisible characters after 'edition'. Read them in order and wrap the code in MFANO braces. https://0xrick.github.io/lists/stego/#unicode-text-steganography

STEG-02.title: The unpunched ticket
STEG-02.hint: Isolate the PNG's alpha channel and stretch its contrast. Count the dots per row from top to bottom. Put t1ck3t_ before the three digits inside the flag. https://0xrick.github.io/lists/stego/#stegsolve

STEG-03.title: The sound desk's archive slip
STEG-03.hint: Read the Archive phrase in steganography/evidence/studio-cue.txt. Use it to extract the WAV's note with Steghide and wrap the Archive code in MFANO braces. https://0xrick.github.io/lists/stego/#steghide
